title: Initial counter state
statement: Let $A$ be counting-sort arguments, let $kf$ assign a natural-number key to each index, and let $mu'$ be an integer-valued memory map. If the first $A.nb+1$ counter cells are zero, then the cell at address $A.cnt$ contains $0$, and for each key $t<A.nb$, the cell at address $A.cnt+(t+1)$ contains the number of indices $i<0$ for which $kf(i)=t$.
hypotheses_covered: The memory map is zero at every counter address $A.cnt+t$ for $t<A.nb+1$
replaced:
Let $A$ be a set of counting-sort parameters, with key bound $A.nb$ and counter-array
start $A.cnt$, and let $kf:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ assign a key to each index. If
$\mu':\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ is zero at every counter position $A.cnt+t$ for
$t<A.nb+1$, then $\mu'(A.cnt)=0$ and, for every $t<A.nb$, the counter at position
$A.cnt+(t+1)$ equals the number of indices $i<0$ whose key is $t$.
